features.description: Cost-lever ship for implementer dispatch — D007 fix. Original framing hypothesized the implementer prompt template was bloated; inventory found the template is already ~5KB (plan_id + feature dict + steps + forbidden/required lists). The actual cost driver is the agent's autonomous tool-use loop: `tokens_in` sums input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens, and prior tool results (e.g. a full `pytest -q` ~1800-line output) get re-read into context on every subsequent turn at the cache_read rate. Two safe levers shipped (OAuth-compatible — `--bare` was considered and rejected because it disables OAuth/keychain auth): (a) every Claude CLI dispatch gets `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`, moving cwd/env/git/memory paths from cached system prompt to first user message for better cross-dispatch cache reuse; (b) implementer prompt embeds a TEST_DISCIPLINE_NOTE instructing targeted tests over full sweeps with explicit rationale (cache_read accumulation). Auditor prompt untouched. Re-measurement is a follow-up dispatch — acceptance does NOT pin a hard token threshold because the actual reduction depends on agent behavior shaped by the prompt note, not prompt-template byte size.
steps: Inventory the implementer prompt template — found it's already ~5KB; D007 hypothesis was based on wrong cause.
Locate cost driver: `tokens_in` includes cache_read_input_tokens from cumulative tool-use turns.
Add `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` to ClaudeCLIExecutor argv on every dispatch.
Add TEST_DISCIPLINE_NOTE module-level constant + thread into both iter0 and iterN implementer prompt paths.
Update test_f005b_executor_argv.py to account for the new flag position in argv.
Add new fixture tests covering both levers (test_v3_f002_cost_levers.py).
Document the discovery + lever choice in plan 2026-05-11-001 decisions.jsonl (D015/D016).
features.acceptance: (1) Every Claude CLI dispatch passes `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` (verified via test_v3_f002_cost_levers + updated test_f005b_executor_argv). (2) TEST_DISCIPLINE_NOTE is exported from prompts and appears in both iter0 and iterN implementer prompts. (3) Implementer prompt total size stays < 10KB (size invariant pinned). (4) Full orchestrate sweep stays green. (5) Parent plan D-entries document the prompt-template-vs-tool-use-loop discovery — re-baseline what 'good' looks like for future v4 work.

features.description: Add `spec_ambiguity` class to no_progress taxonomy — D008 fix. The v0 6-class taxonomy (feature_defect / regression / interpretive_disagreement / redundant / already-known / spec-clarification) has no class for the most common audit terminal-non-success seen in practice: a documentation/placement finding that's neither a defect nor a real disagreement, just a spec gap. Add `spec_ambiguity` as a 7th class with pattern-match rules: severity in {low, medium} AND category in {documentation, naming, convention, placement}. The classifier emits this class non-blocking with recommended_action 'Operator-review for spec gap; patch spec then resume or accept implementer's reading'. Existing 6 classes preserved.
steps: Read scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/auditor_taxonomy.py + the no_progress_classification path.
Add `spec_ambiguity` enum value + classification rule (severity ∈ {low,medium} ∧ category ∈ {documentation, naming, convention, placement}).
Update the recommended_action template for the new class.
Mark `spec_ambiguity` non-blocking (operator can resume without manual review). Open question for D-entry: should it be non-blocking or just lower-friction-blocking?
Fixture tests: documentation findings → spec_ambiguity; security/correctness findings still → existing classes; previously-`unknown` cases now classify correctly.
Reclassify the plan 010 F001 iteration 1 finding against the new taxonomy as evidence.
features.acceptance: (1) `spec_ambiguity` class exists in auditor_taxonomy. (2) Plan 010 F001 iteration 1 finding reclassifies to spec_ambiguity (not unknown). (3) Fixture tests cover the new pattern + don't regress existing classifications. (4) Recommended_action template documents the operator-review-or-accept workflow.

features.description: Operator-resolved close-out workflow — D009 fix. When a volley terminates stopped_no_progress and operator review judges the audit finding as non-defect (e.g., spec_ambiguity from F003), there's no clean path to close the feature. Currently: operator must clear breaker:no_progress AND manually author a closeout-memo at a path the supervisor doesn't tell them about (evidence/closeout-memo.md) AND manually flip features.json. Add a `dontpanic close --operator-resolved <plan-id> <feature-id> --reason <class>` CLI that: (a) auto-generates a minimal closeout-memo template, (b) clears breaker:no_progress in gate-state.json, (c) writes a signoff envelope marking the feature operator_resolved with class. Document the path conventions in the INBOX event when stopped_no_progress fires so operator sees the recommended next command inline.
steps: Read signoff_writer.py + the current close-out flow.
Add `dontpanic close --operator-resolved <plan-id> <feature-id> --reason <class>` to cli.py.
Template generates a minimal closeout-memo with status: operator_resolved, class, summary lifted from the latest auditor envelope.
Wire breaker:no_progress clear + signoff envelope write into one transaction.
Update the no_progress INBOX event template to include the recommended `dontpanic close --operator-resolved ...` command inline.
Smoke test against plan 010 F001 fixture (don't touch the real plan — it's already closed).
features.acceptance: (1) `dontpanic close --operator-resolved <plan> <feature> --reason <class>` works end-to-end. (2) Generates closeout-memo template. (3) Clears breaker:no_progress + writes signoff in one transaction. (4) INBOX no_progress event surfaces the recommended close command inline. (5) Smoke test against a synthetic fixture (not the real plan 010 — it's already closed via the existing path).
